subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is brought in during an upper respiratory infection with lethargy and vomiting after 20 hours of poor intake. Glucose is 30 mg/dL, lactate 9.4 mmol/L, pH 7.28, and beta-hydroxybutyrate is elevated; the liver edge is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin, and uric acid is normal. His older brother had a similar episode of fasting hypoglycemia.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible for these recurrent episodes?
explanation_correct: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 1 is one of the four irreversible gluconeogenic enzymes and is inhibited by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and activated by citrate. Its deficiency blocks gluconeogenesis from all precursors, causing fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis and ketosis that is typically triggered by fasting or infection, while the absence of hyperuricemia and marked hypertriglyceridemia helps distinguish it from glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency.

explanation_incorrect.A: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (von Gierke disease) also causes fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis, but it presents earlier with massive hepatomegaly, hyperuricemia, and hypertriglyceridemia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency causes lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia with neurologic disease, but the lactic acidosis is present even when fed and is not typically an episodic disorder triggered by infection.
explanation_incorrect.D: Liver glycogen phosphorylase deficiency (Hers disease) causes fasting hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly, but lactic acidosis is not a feature because gluconeogenesis is intact.
explanation_incorrect.E: Phosphofructokinase-1 deficiency is a rare glycolytic defect that causes hemolytic anemia and exercise intolerance, not fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis.

educationalObjective: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 1 deficiency blocks gluconeogenesis and causes recurrent fasting hypoglycemia with lactic acidosis and ketosis triggered by fasting or infection.
